column2: Gameplay is king. If you have funny or beautiful gameplay it does well. Having a funny video like watch out for goblins doesn't mean it will convert well to wishlists. The more pure gameplay it goes viral for the more it correlates to added followers
try showcasing your game with a 15 seconds of our gameplay but also one or two min clips
Featuring trailers can work.
Time lapses of your game's progress works very well. Or before and after blank months/years
Showing how you fixed something in your game
Responding to negative comments to get people to root for your underdog story works well

Sometimes if a tiktok does really and you do it again but slightly different, it goes viral again, sometimes it doesn't. Don't give up after a couple tries, sometimes the same video is made over and over again and it goes viral and other times not. However if you get no views / engagement, not a great sign
Some really indie games just use their personal tiktok accounts instead of the games
Even the best games with lots of viral videos still would release videso that only got a couple hundred or thousand views. You won't always go viral
Not many games were a surprise. Most looked good enough or had an interesting design to go viral. Only a few surprising ones that won through humor or showing an interesting bug fix
You don't have to say anything, you can use ai voiceover or just put text on the screen.
Adding to the game through TikTok Comments, some even built their game through comments
Not a ton of over the top profressionalism, rarely any tiktok trending style content, only a few capcut memes
If a game does well because of gameplay, typically they have numerous viral videos where if a game goes viral for something funny then they often don't repeat
It seems that videos that go viral because of the game itself and not because it's funny convert to more wishlists. Sort through video types to try and confirm it with data
Plunder is an interesting case study where he got a ton more views on YT shorts than on Tiktok, 10k wishlists
290 followers per 1mil views - 2000ish wishlists gain
Do another table to just show results of upcoming games since already released games don't often get more followers
Many genres went viral but of course there are some trends. Horror games, social co-op funny games, cozy games, cozy building games, survival games, simulation games like car ones?
Showing your early game vs late game such as combat or how your buildings change, etc.

A ridiculous & stupid mechanic works - cutting down a tree with a dead body, npc farting when you try to pickpocket them, crazy glitches, impossible vehicles, jiggle phyics, ridiculous drug references, etc. Things you wouldn't normally see or have allowed in a polished AA or AAA game.
Asking a feedback question works "how does this look" "what do you think"
Comparing yourself to other popular games can work but only found a few examples
If you're super indie, use that to your advantage. Sharing from a first person perspective, or saything things like me and my boyfriend are making this game...
